method: Manually inspected full current cards for the listed targeted candidates from catalog-candidates.json. This is a limited relevant-neighbor review, not a claim that every ranked item or all 11,000 cards was manually read.

reviewed.review: Both ask an SI unit, but the measured quantities and correct units are different; no tested force fact repeats.
Same elementary unit-question format, distinct base quantity (length versus force).
Neighbor asks which constant defines the metre; target asks for the numerical vacuum speed. Related SI relation, but not the same requested fact.
Neighbor tests whether electromagnetic light can travel in vacuum; target tests its speed. Complementary distinct properties.
Neighbor asks which instrument separates wavelengths; target asks the physical wavelength-dependent effect in droplets. Instrument versus mechanism.
Neighbor defines index as a ratio of wave speeds; target concerns wavelength dependence that splits colors. Related optics, distinct relation.
Neighbor defines force-time impulse and momentum change; target asks paired forces in an interaction. Different law and tested relation.
Neighbor defines current as charge per time; target asks conventional current direction relative to electron drift. Distinct quantity definition versus sign convention.
Neighbor asks instrument and series connection; target asks direction convention. Device procedure versus charge-direction convention.
Neighbor asks freezing point at normal pressure; target asks boiling point at standard pressure. Different phase transition and temperature; no direct/inverse duplicate.
Neighbor establishes that electromagnetic light propagates in vacuum; target explains why mechanical sound cannot. Contrast pair, distinct correct fact.
Neighbor identifies the first-arriving seismic P-wave; it concerns seismic travel order, not the need for a propagation medium in vacuum.
Neighbor asks weight direction; target distinguishes mass from weight and their dependency/units. Same term, different tested relation.
Neighbor defines mass as amount/inertia; target explicitly contrasts mass with gravitational weight. Related mass fact, but not the distinction tested.
Neighbor defines absolute density as mass per volume; target tests the distinct dimensionless specific-gravity ratio to water. Related foundational concept, no repeated mass/volume definition.
Neighbor names seawater mass per volume; target interprets a ratio against reference water. Related density, distinct tested relation.
Neighbor is dry-soil bulk density including pore volume; target is the unitless ratio to reference water. Different quantity and application.
Neighbor asks which element has a high absolute density; target interprets relative density 0.8. Distinct fact.
Boyle-law duplicate applied to an earlier draft of this selected ID; the final candidate no longer tests pressure/volume and is distinct.

unreviewedCandidatePolicy: All other ranked candidates remain unadjudicated. Full manual relevant-neighbor coverage is not complete.
